title: A Look at the AI Hyperscalers
summary: Hyperscaler capital spending challenges cash generation.
coverage_note: All numbered text blocks and image labels read. Material theses, forecasts and explanations are included; routine holdings lists, incidental statistics, company descriptions and boilerplate are excluded. Chart pixels were not inspected.

claims.reason: Subsequent reserve-management purchases support the diagnosis that reserve demand was approaching the ample-reserves boundary. SOFR can also reflect collateral supply, dealer constraints and quarter-end effects; one spread is not an economy-wide liquidity measure.
claims.mechanism_assessment: Outcome evidence does not independently identify causation.

evidence.title: Reserve management purchases statement
evidence.finding: Fed directed purchases of Treasury bills, or maturities up to three years if needed, to maintain ample reserves. Initial reserve-management purchases began in December 2025.

evidence.title: Time-varying reserve demand curve
evidence.finding: Study estimates reserve satiation above 12-13% of bank assets using 2010-24 data. Reserve demand shifts over time; the estimate is not a binding fixed regulatory minimum.

claims.reason: The rule change can reduce capital costs of Treasury intermediation, but SLR measures Tier 1 capital relative to total leverage exposure. It does not let banks multiply a fixed reserve base in the way stated. The distinction matters when forecasting which balance sheet constraint binds.
claims.mechanism_assessment: Outcome evidence does not independently identify causation.

evidence.title: Final enhanced supplementary leverage rule
evidence.finding: Rule recalibrated leverage capital requirements for the largest banks, effective April 1, 2026 with optional January 1 adoption, to reduce disincentives to Treasury intermediation. This is a capital backstop, not a reserve requirement.

evidence.title: Supplementary leverage ratio denominator rule
evidence.finding: Supplementary leverage exposure includes on-balance-sheet assets and specified off-balance-sheet exposures; the capital standard is not a ratio of loans to reserve balances.

claims.reason: Holding other Fed balance-sheet items constant, lower Treasury cash increases another liability such as reserves. Actual reserve changes also depend on reverse repos, currency and asset holdings; no date or realized amount was specified.
claims.mechanism_assessment: Outcome evidence does not independently identify causation.

claims.reason: The margin and funding-cost mechanism is plausible, but establishing that it drove the observed equity weakness needs leverage, funding, collateral and flow evidence. A borrowing aggregate alone does not identify forced selling.

framework_lessons: Capital, reserves and free cash flow require distinct definitions.
assessment: The warning about infrastructure spending translated into observable cash pressure at Alphabet, Meta and Oracle. The blanket funding explanation was too broad at publication, and the SLR explanation confuses capital with reserves. The global easing thesis also diverged across central banks. Long-horizon AI and gold outcomes remain open.
verification_limitations: Retrieved 2026-11-07; publication-date wording is not authenticated.

Public market series are available, but not every investment claim has a defined horizon or reconciled corporate-action-adjusted return. Unverified outcomes remain unscored; macro data use latest available vintages.
